newsitem.title: USA: N.J. lawmakers set schedule for budget hearings.
newsitem.headline: N.J. lawmakers set schedule for budget hearings.

text.p: New Jersey lawmakers set March 5 as the first public hearing on Gov. Christine Whitman's proposed fiscal 1998 budget.
The joint hearing of the Senate Budget and Appropriations and Assembly Appropriations committees will take place at the State House in Trenton.
Public hearings are also set for March 12 in Hoboken and March 26 in Blackwood.
State Treasurer Brian Clymer and the Office of Legislative Services are scheduled to present a budget overview on March 25 in Trenton.

Clymer is expected to be grilled by lawmakers on Whitman's controversial plan to sell $2.9 billion of taxable bonds to fully fund the state's pension system. The plan provides $647 million of one-shot budget relief to the fiscal 1997 and 1998 spending plans.
Lawmakers, including key Republican allies of the governor, have questioned the wisdom of selling what would amount to the largest-ever bond sale by the state.
